what: SHA-256 of the PCM samples of Minesweeper's recorded sounds (the WAV's data chunk, i.e. the file from byte 44 on; the 44-byte header is not hashed because it carries no sound).
why: The recording itself is not committed: media files (.wav) are refused by the repository's pre-push guard, and a fixture a person can open is not needed, only a strict proof that the sounds are unchanged. Re-recorded after the 1x font tables shrank: the binaries lost 15 bytes (3417 to 3402, and 3445 to 3430), which moves instruction timing slightly, so each sound begins a fraction of a sample earlier or later inside the WAV's sample windows. The WAV averages the machine's level over each sample's window, so a burst's edge values change a little while its note, length and peak do not. The random seed is not the cause: the test pokes SEED=$5EED, RANDOMIZE therefore takes the SEED branch, never reads the counter, and RSEED ends up $5EED in both builds. Measured: every cue's pitch within one zero crossing, its length within one sample, its peak identical (20160); the recording is byte-identical run to run, and byte-identical when an unrelated delay in the script moves by five frames.
command: node cli/cloadm.js -m dragon64 --program minesweeper --frames 30 --poke $3003=$5E,$ED --type ' ' --frames 20 --wav OUT.wav --type ' ' --frames 20 --type '{RIGHT}{DOWN}F' --frames 20 --type '{UP}{RIGHT}{RIGHT}' --frames 5 --type F --frames 10 --type F --frames 10 --type ' ' --frames 60 --wav-stop
listen: To hear it, run that command with OUT.wav set to a path outside this repository (the same sequence tests/games.test.js runs). Nothing is written into the repo.
note: Phase shift is expected and documented; the sound itself is unchanged.
